title: Selection Sort
intuition: Finds the smallest unsorted element in each pass and swaps it directly into its sorted slot.
whyExists: Minimizes memory write operations ($O(n)$ swaps total), making it advantageous when write cycles are expensive.
analogy: Selecting cards from an unsorted hand: scanning the entire hand for the lowest value and placing it first.
coreIdea: Maintains a partition between a sorted prefix [0..i-1] and an unsorted suffix [i..n-1]. In pass i, it scans the suffix to find the minimum value's index minIdx and executes a single swap between a[i] and a[minIdx].

complexity.reason: Always scans the entire remaining unsorted suffix regardless of initial ordering.

pitfalls: Selection sort is NOT stable in its default form because long-distance swaps can reorder equal elements.
Updating the minimum value without saving its index minIdx.
Comparing against a fixed value rather than the moving minimum.
